payload.title: Piecewise function: continuity, differentiability, tangent line, average value of the derivative

data.definition: f(x) = x^2 -4x for x <= 1; f(x) = -4sqrt(x) +1 for x > 1

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Let $f$ be the function defined by $f(x)=\begin{cases} x^{2}-4x, & x\le 1\\ -4\sqrt{x}+1, & x>1 \end{cases}$. Show that $f$ is continuous at $x=1$.
parts.model_answer: f(1) = 1 -4 = -3; the left limit is -3; the right limit is -4(1) +1 = -3; the one-sided limits equal f(1), so f is continuous at x = 1.

rubric_rows.criterion: Evaluates f(1) and the left-hand limit
Right-hand limit equal to f(1): the condition for continuity is met

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Is $f$ differentiable at $x=1$? Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: For x < 1, f'(x) = 2x -4, so the left derivative at 1 is -2; for x > 1, f'(x) = -4/(2 sqrt x), so the right derivative at 1 is -2. They are equal and f is continuous, so f is differentiable at x = 1.

rubric_rows.criterion: Left-hand derivative at x = 1
Right-hand derivative at x = 1
Justification and conclusion: the one-sided derivatives are equal, so f is differentiable (yes)

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Write an equation for the line tangent to the curve $y=f(x)$ at $x=1$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Uses the slope f'(1) from part (b)

parts.label: d

rubric_rows.criterion: Uses the Fundamental Theorem: the integral of f' from 0 to 4 is f(4) - f(0)
Value of the average
